# Commercially available humanoid robots
Many humanoid robots are announced, demonstrated, or in pilot — far fewer are buyable today.
This page filters the catalog to platforms with active commercial procurement channels.

### Apollo
Apollo is a bipedal humanoid robot from Apptronik aimed at automating tasks in industrial and commercial environments.
...
### Which humanoid robots can I buy today?
The shortest list: Unitree platforms (G1, H1) for research/education; Fourier GR-1 for research; some Chinese platforms via direct order.
Most flagship US platforms (Atlas, Figure 03, Apollo) are deployment-partner-only as of mid-2026.

results.title: Humanoid Robot Industry Report 2026

results.snippet:
The Unitree G1, at around $16,000, is available online, while Agility Robotics' Digit, costing about $250,000, targets industrial clients like Amazon.
1X's Neo Gamma is opening pre-orders for home use at $20,000 or $499/month, with 2026 shipping.
Other models like Figure O3 and Agibot A2 serve enterprise or industrial roles.
Notably, Tesla Optimus and Boston Dynamics Atlas remain unavailable for purchase.
...
Humanoid robots are moving from science fiction into the real world, with several models now available for homes, research labs and industrial deployments.
...
The Unitree G1 is one of the few humanoid robots that can easily be ordered by anyone today.
...
Most of the humanoid robots that are available today aren’t as easily accessible as the G1, and purchases are negotiated through enterprise procurement channels rather than websites.
...
Neo Gamma, from 1X, has been available to companies running enterprise deployments for a while, but pre-orders have just opened up for individual private purchasers.
Neo Gamma, standing at 5ft 5in tall and weighing 30kg, is among the first commercially available humanoids designed specifically for the home.
...
Figure AI’s general-purpose humanoid is another model that’s apparently available to buy, although this is through enterprise partnership and piloting channels rather than retail.
...
Agibot, from Shanghai-based Zhiyuan Robotics, can be purchased directly from its website today.
...
Boston Dynamics’ electric Atlas is one of the most advanced humanoid platforms in the world, but it is not available to ordinary customers.

results.title: Which humanoid robot actually works today?

content.text:
“Commercially available” ranges from robots you can order directly to enterprise-only systems sold through pilots or deployment contracts. **The clearest options as of late 2026 are:**

- **Unitree R1 and G1** — orderable through Unitree’s store for research, education, and development; the G1 may be backordered. [15][17]
- **Unitree H1 and H2** — commercial platforms generally sold through business or institutional channels. [6][10]
- **Agility Robotics Digit** — available for warehouse and industrial deployments, typically through enterprise agreements or Robotics-as-a-Service. [2][6]
- **UBTECH Walker-series robots, including Walker S2** — offered for industrial and service applications; UBTECH reported substantial 2026 sales of full-size humanoids. [2][20]
- **AgiBot models, including A2 and A3** — commercially marketed, with reported deliveries of A3 units and direct-purchase channels for some models. [4][8]
- **Fourier GR-1** — sold mainly for research and healthcare-related use. [6][7]
- **Engineered Arts Ameca** — commercially offered for events, entertainment, and human–robot interaction, including sale or rental. [4][6]
- **1X NEO** — available by preorder, not a broadly in-stock home robot; the company lists a $20,000 early-access option and planned 2026 deliveries. [11][12]

Other robots—including **Figure, Apptronik Apollo, and Boston Dynamics Atlas**—have commercial pilots, partner deployments, or announced production, but generally aren’t straightforward retail purchases. [2][6][8]
